label: June 1–7
title: “My Heart Rejoiceth in the Lord” —  Ruth; 1 Samuel 1

items.text: Life is often full of delays and detours that take us in unexpected directions. Ruth and Hannah surely understood this. As you read about their journeys, consider the faith they must have had to travel their unexpected paths, and learn to say with Hannah, 'My heart rejoiceth in the Lord.'
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: Jesus Christ can turn tragedy into triumph. As you read Ruth’s story, notice how the Lord turned her desperate situation into great blessings. Consider how both Ruth and Boaz were like Jesus Christ in redeeming and blessing her life, even in sorrow.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: I can trust that God will guide and help me regardless of my situation. Like Ruth and Naomi after loss, or Hannah longing for blessings, we can show our faith in God. Everyone who turns to the Savior receives His help and guidance, and we can learn to trust Him during difficult times.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: To receive the Lord’s help, I need to trust Him and obey His commandments. The Israelites learned that simply possessing the ark did not guarantee protection. We learn from their experiences, and from Hannah’s poem of praise, how to seek and receive the Lord’s guidance and protection through faith and obedience.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: I can hear and obey the voice of the Lord. Like Samuel, we must learn to recognize the Lord’s voice. By studying His word and seeking His Spirit, we can discern His promptings. President Nelson reminds us that God truly wants to speak to us, inviting us to hear and obey His voice.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: When enemies attacked, the Israelites thought possessing the ark would protect them. Their failure teaches us that true protection comes from trusting and obeying God, not just from sacred objects. We learn from Israel’s efforts to regain the Lord’s favor in 1 Samuel 7.

Hannah’s poem of praise in 1 Samuel 2 is filled with profound insights. Her words could have helped Eli’s sons and the rest of the Israelites understand the power of trusting in the Lord. Her example teaches us to rejoice in Him, even amidst sorrow or unmet desires.

God’s power is not limited by our circumstances. Ruth, a foreigner, embraced Israel’s faith and found redemption through Boaz, a type of Christ. Her story powerfully illustrates how the Lord can turn tragedy into triumph and bless those who cleave unto Him.

We are not alone in our trials. Like Ruth, who faced widowhood and displacement, or Hannah, who grieved over her inability to have children, we too experience difficult paths. Through faith and turning to the Savior, we can find His help and guidance, learning to say, 'My heart rejoiceth in the Lord.'

Recognizing the Lord’s voice requires learning and obedience. Samuel, a young boy, learned to hear and respond to the Lord. By studying His word and diligently seeking His Spirit, we can also learn to recognize His voice and follow His divine guidance in our lives.
